question: What is a health check, and what is the difference between active and passive health checking?
answer_hinglish:
Health check ka matlab hai load balancer ka yeh pata lagana ki koi upstream traffic lene ke layak hai ya nahi. Do tarike hain. Active health check mein proxy khud timer par har upstream ko ek chhoti request bhejta hai (jaise GET /health) aur jawab dekhta hai, user traffic se bilkul alag. Passive health check mein proxy asli user requests ke nateejon ko dekhta hai: agar ek upstream se connection baar baar fail ho raha hai, toh use rotation se hata do.

Active ka fayda: problem user se pehle pakdi ja sakti hai, aur jo server hata diya gaya uske wapas aane ka pata bina traffic ke chal jata hai. Nuksan: extra probe traffic, aur /health endpoint asli kaam ko poori tarah represent nahi karta. Passive ka fayda: koi extra load nahi aur woh asli raaste ko hi dekhta hai. Nuksan: detect karne ke liye kuch asli users ko pehle failure jhelna padta hai.

Is project mein dono hain. Passive hamesha on hai (`reportFailure` aur `reportSuccess` in balancer.ts), active tab on hota hai jab `HEALTH_PATH` set ho (`HealthChecker` in health.ts). Dono milke kaam karte hain, aur dono ke alag tests hain.
why_needed: Mare hue ya sust server ko pehchan ke traffic usse hatana, taaki users ko errors na milein.
real_world_analogy: Active: doctor har subah sab ka checkup karta hai. Passive: aap tab dhyan dete ho jab koi dukaan baar baar band mili.
how_it_works: Active: timer par probe, thresholds ke saath state flip. Passive: har asli request ke result se counter update, threshold par ejection.
in_this_project: Passive: balancer.ts::Balancer.reportFailure aur reportSuccess, proxy.ts mein call hote hain. Active: health.ts::HealthChecker.
code_example: HEALTH_PATH=/health UPSTREAM=http://10.0.0.5:3000,http://10.0.0.6:3000 node dist/index.js
advantages: Dono milke jaldi detection aur recovery dete hain
Passive ke liye extra load nahi
disadvantages: Active mein probe load aur shallow endpoint ka risk
Passive mein pehle kuch users ko failure
common_mistakes: Sirf active ya sirf passive par bharosa
Health endpoint ko hamesha 200 return karne dena

question: When does this proxy answer 502, 503 and 504, and how do you tell them apart?
answer_hinglish:
Teeno 5xx hain lekin alag matlab. 502 Bad Gateway: proxy ne upstream se baat karne ki koshish ki lekin valid jawab nahi mila: connection refused ya reset. 504 Gateway Timeout: connection hua lekin upstream ne time par jawab nahi diya (idle timeout) ya connection hi time par nahi bana (connect timeout). 503 Service Unavailable: proxy ne koshish hi nahi ki kyunki koi upstream available hi nahi tha (sab unhealthy ya ejected).

503 ke saath hum `Retry-After: 1` bhi bhejte hain, matlab client ek second baad dobara koshish kar sakta hai. Test `answers 503 with Retry-After when no upstream is available` isko check karta hai: pehla request 502 deta hai (jo upstream ko eject karta hai), doosra 503.

Jab alag alag codes dikhte hain toh debugging aasan hoti hai. 502 ki baarish: upstream process down ya galat port. 504: upstream zinda lekin slow ya hung. 503: poora pool bahar, health checks ya ejection ki wajah se, toh health events ke logs dekhne chahiye. Dhyan: agar upstream khud 500 ya 503 bheje, toh proxy use as-is client ko deta hai; woh proxy ka apna error nahi hai.
why_needed: Alag failures ko alag signal dena taaki operators sahi jagah dekhein.
real_world_analogy: 502: phone mila par awaaz kharab. 504: phone uthaya par kisi ne bola hi nahi. 503: koi number hi available nahi tha, to dial hi nahi kiya.
how_it_works: Error handler error type dekhta hai: timeout classes -> 504, baaki connection errors -> 502. NoHealthyUpstreamError (balancer) -> 503.
in_this_project: proxy.ts::sendError; balancer.ts::NoHealthyUpstreamError; tests in resilience.test.ts.
advantages: Clear signal for debugging and alerting
503 client ko retry hint deta hai
disadvantages: Clients ko 5xx ke farak ki samajh honi chahiye
Upstream ke apne 5xx ko proxy ke errors se mix kiya ja sakta hai
common_mistakes: Sab ko 500 ya 502 bana dena
503 ko 502 ke saath mix karna

question: What does idempotent mean, and why does it decide whether a request can be retried?
answer_hinglish:
Idempotent ka matlab: wahi request ek baar bhejo ya kai baar, server ki final state wahi rehti hai. GET, HEAD, OPTIONS safe aur idempotent hain: sirf padhte hain. POST aam taur par idempotent nahi hai: ek order ya payment banane wali POST do baar chale toh do order ya do charge ban sakte hain.

Retry kab khatarnak hai: maan lo proxy ne POST upstream ko bheja, upstream ne kaam kar liya lekin jawab bhejne se pehle connection toot gaya. Proxy ko pata nahi ki kaam hua ya nahi. Agar woh retry kare toh kaam do baar ho sakta hai. GET mein yeh problem nahi.

Is project mein retry sirf GET, HEAD aur OPTIONS ke liye hai, aur sirf tab jab body bhi na ho. PUT aur DELETE spec mein idempotent hain, lekin hum unhe bhi retry nahi karte: conservative rakha, kyunki PUT ki body stream hoti hai aur dobara bheji nahi ja sakti. Test `a POST with NO body is still not retried` yeh pakadta hai, aur maine retry check hata ke dekha ki test fail hota hai.
why_needed: Retry se duplicate side effects (double charge) rokna.
real_world_analogy: Lift ka button: do baar dabaane se lift ek hi baar aati hai (idempotent). Order button do baar dabaane se do pizza aa jaate hain.
how_it_works: Method ke semantics se decide hota hai. Proxy ko request ka matlab nahi pata, isliye method ke basis par safe set chuna.
in_this_project: proxy.ts::isReplayable GET/HEAD/OPTIONS aur body-less check karta hai.
code_example: if (method !== "GET" && method !== "HEAD" && method !== "OPTIONS") return false;
advantages: Duplicate side effects ka risk nahi
disadvantages: PUT/DELETE ko retry nahi karte: kuch safe retries chhoot jaati hain
common_mistakes: POST ko retry karna kyunki 'body chhoti hai'
Sochna ki idempotent matlab body-less

question: How does passive ejection decide to remove an upstream, and when does it come back?
answer_hinglish:
Rule: consecutive connection-level failures count hote hain. `ejectAfter` (default 3) failures lagatar hon toh target `ejectMs` (default 10 second) ke liye rotation se bahar. Is dauran `isAvailable()` false deta hai aur balancer use skip karta hai. Time poora hone par target wapas available ho jata hai, bina kisi probe ke.

Yahan ek chhoti trick hai: ejection ke waqt `failures` ko `ejectAfter - 1` par set kar dete hain. Matlab wapas aane ke baad EK hi aur failure usko turant dobara eject kar deta hai (ek trial request), jab ki ek success `failures` ko 0 kar deta hai aur woh poori tarah wapas. Is se bimaar server ko baar baar poore 3 failures ka mauka nahi milta.

Dhyan do: failures CONSECUTIVE hone chahiye. Beech mein ek success streak tod deta hai (test `a success resets the streak` aur integration test `failures must be consecutive on real traffic`). Aur jo requests ejection se pehle hi flight mein thi unke baad ke failures ejection ko lamba nahi karte. Yeh sab fake clock ke saath unit tests mein check hota hai, bina real waiting ke.
why_needed: Mare hue server ko tezi se hatana, aur theek hone par automatically wapas lena.
real_world_analogy: Gende ko red card: kuch der bahar, phir wapas, aur wapas aane par pehli galti par seedha dobara bahar.
how_it_works: Per-target counter failures aur ejectedUntil timestamp. isAvailable(now) = healthy && now >= ejectedUntil.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::reportFailure, reportSuccess, isAvailable. Tests: health-state.test.ts 'passive ejection'.
advantages: Single-trial recovery bimaar server ko bachata hai
disadvantages: Defaults production ke liye tune nahi kiye
Time-based: poore time ke liye ek achha server bhi bahar reh sakta hai agar galti se eject hua
common_mistakes: Total failures count karna, consecutive nahi
Ejection ke dauran stragglers se timer badhana

question: Why does an HTTP 500 from the upstream not count as a failure for passive ejection?
answer_hinglish:
500 ka matlab hai upstream tak connection pahuncha, uska application chala, aur usne jawab diya, bas jawab 'error' tha. Server reachable hai. Ejection ka maqsad unreachable ya mare hue servers ko hatana hai, application bugs ko nahi. Agar 500 par bhi eject karte toh ek buggy endpoint (jaise ek report jo crash hoti hai) poore server ko rotation se hata deta, jabki baaki endpoints theek chal rahe hain. Isse ek chhoti problem poore pool ki outage ban sakti hai: agar sab servers par wahi bug ho, toh sab eject ho jaate aur 503 milta.

Is project mein `reportFailure` sirf connection-level events par chalta hai: refused, reset, timeout, ya response beech mein kata. HTTP status ka koi asar nahi. Test `an upstream that answers 500 is NOT ejected` paanch baar 500 aane par bhi 500 hi return hone ko check karta hai (kabhi 503 nahi).

Trade-off: sach mein kharab server jo har request par 500 deta hai woh rotation mein rahega. Uske liye success-rate based outlier detection chahiye (agle sawaal mein), jo abhi implement nahi hai, ya active health check jo /health par 500 dekhe.
why_needed: Application bugs ko infrastructure outages se alag rakhna, aur cascading ejection se bachna.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan khuli hai lekin ek item khatam: dukaan band nahi kar dete. Dukaan ka darwaza hi band ho toh baat alag hai.
how_it_works: Passive health sirf transport-level errors dekhta hai. Status code application ka mamla hai.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: reportSuccess on response (any status); reportFailure on request error ya incomplete body. Test: an upstream that answers 500 is NOT ejected.
advantages: Ek buggy endpoint poore server ko hatata nahi
disadvantages: Hamesha-500 server rotation mein rehta hai
Success-rate detection nahi hai

Sochna ki status code ka kabhi koi role nahi

question: Why do active health checks need several results in a row before changing a target's state?
answer_hinglish:
Network mein ek akeli probe kai wajah se fail ho sakti hai: ek packet lost, ek slow GC pause, ek chhoti si load spike. Agar ek hi failure par server ko 'down' maan lein, toh woh baar baar up-down hota rahega (flapping), aur har flip par traffic idhar udhar hota hai, aur logs aur alerts ka shor hota hai. Isliye threshold: `unhealthyThreshold` (default 2) lagatar fail hone par hi down, aur `healthyThreshold` (default 2) lagatar pass hone par hi wapas up.

Streak ek counter hai: pass aane par ok++ aur bad=0; fail par bad++ aur ok=0. Test `a pass in between resets the failure streak (no flapping on a lone blip)` fail, pass, fail, pass sequence dene par target healthy rehta hai. Aur `a down target needs healthyThreshold passes in a row to come back` recovery ko check karta hai.

Maine threshold ko 1 kar ke dekha: do tests fail hue. Trade-off: zyada threshold matlab slow detection (interval x threshold seconds, default 5s x 2 = 10s tak). Yeh numbers theory ke hisaab se hain, maine real traffic par measure nahi kiye.
why_needed: Flapping aur false alarms se bachna.
real_world_analogy: Ek baar chheenk aane par chhutti nahi lete, do din lagatar bukhar ho toh doctor ke paas jaate hain.
how_it_works: Per-target {ok, bad} streak. Threshold paar hone par balancer.setHealthy().
in_this_project: health.ts::HealthChecker.record; tests in healthchecker.test.ts (HealthChecker thresholds).
code_example:
if (ok) { streak.ok++; streak.bad = 0; if (!target.healthy && streak.ok >= this.healthyThreshold) { /* up */ } }
else { streak.bad++; streak.ok = 0; if (target.healthy && streak.bad >= this.unhealthyThreshold) { /* down */ } }
disadvantages: Detection slow: interval x threshold
Defaults production ke liye tune nahi kiye
common_mistakes: Threshold 1 rakhna
Down aur up ke liye alag thresholds ki zarurat ko ignore karna

question: Why combine active and passive checks instead of picking one?
answer_hinglish:
Dono ki kamzoriyaan alag hain, isliye saath mein ek doosre ko cover karte hain. Passive akela: ek server jo kal raat se band hai, uske liye pehle kuch users ko failure jhelna padta hai tab detect hota hai, aur ejection ke baad uske wapas aane ka pata sirf tab chalta hai jab uspe trial request jaye. Active akela: probe ka /health endpoint theek ho sakta hai jabki asli endpoints toot rahe hon, aur probe interval ke beech (5 second) ek server mar jaye toh us dauran users failure dekhte hain.

Combined: passive turant react karta hai asli failures par (3 failures lagatar), active background mein state sahi rakhta hai aur recovery confirm karta hai. Hamare code mein dono `Balancer` ke state ko badalte hain: active `setHealthy`, passive `ejectedUntil`. `isAvailable` dono ko ek saath dekhta hai. Aur jab active check target ko healthy kare toh passive ejection bhi clear ho jata hai (test `setHealthy ... clears a passive ejection when healthy again`).

Integration test `takes an unhealthy upstream out of rotation and puts it back when it recovers` active path ko asli HTTP servers par end to end chalata hai.
why_needed: Detection speed aur accuracy ka balance.
real_world_analogy: Guard ki raat ki gasht (active) aur CCTV par kisi ko chor dikhna (passive): dono saath mein safety zyada.
how_it_works: Do independent signals, ek hi available/unavailable decision. isAvailable = healthy AND not ejected.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::isAvailable, setHealthy, reportFailure; health.ts::HealthChecker.
disadvantages: Do mechanisms ko samajhna aur tune karna padta hai
common_mistakes: Dono ko ek hi counter mein mix karna
Active ke recovery ko passive ejection ke saath sync na karna

question: Explain the trick of setting failures to ejectAfter minus one at ejection time.
answer_hinglish:
Maan lo `ejectAfter` 3 hai. Normal flow mein ek naya target ko eject hone ke liye 3 failures chahiye. Ejection ke baad jab woh wapas available hota hai, hum chahte hain ki use full 3 mauke na milein: server abhi bhi kharab ho sakta hai, aur har failure ek real user request ki bali hai. Isliye ejection ke samay hum `failures = ejectAfter - 1` (yahan 2) set kar dete hain. Wapas aane par pehli hi failure count ko 3 kar deti hai aur target turant phir eject.

Agar server theek ho gaya hai toh pehli request success hogi, `reportSuccess` `failures` ko 0 kar dega, aur target poori tarah normal ho jata hai. Yeh circuit breaker ke 'half-open' state jaisa hai: ek trial request se faisla.

Yeh implement karna aasan hai (ek line) aur extra state nahi chahiye (koi alag 'half-open' flag nahi). Tests: `after the ejection ends, ONE more failure ejects it again` aur `a success clears the slate so it needs N failures again`. Limitation: trial ke dauran kai requests ek saath aa sakti hain (concurrent), toh ek se zyada user trial ban sakte hain: sirf ek request wala strict half-open abhi nahi hai.
why_needed: Wapas aate hue server ko poora traffic dene se pehle ek chhota test dena.
real_world_analogy: Bimaar player match mein wapas aaye toh pehli galti par turant bench par: pehle sabit karo ki theek ho.
how_it_works: failures counter ko clever tareeke se reuse karna, alag flag ki jagah.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::reportFailure.
code_example:
target.ejectedUntil = now + this.ejectMs;
target.failures = this.ejectAfter - 1;

Bimaar server par kam users bali
disadvantages: Concurrent requests ek se zyada trial ban sakti hain
Clever hone ki wajah se padhne mein subtle

Ejection ke baad flag bhoolna

question: How do the tests exercise time-based ejection without sleeping for 10 seconds?
answer_hinglish:
Balancer ko time source ka reference chahiye, isliye constructor mein `clock` option hai (default `Date.now`). Tests ek chhota fake clock banate hain: `let now = 1000;` aur `clock: () => now`. Phir 'time guzarna' simply `now += 9_999` hai. Koi `setTimeout` ya sleep nahi, isliye 10 second ke ejection ka test milliseconds mein chalta hai aur deterministic hai (kabhi flaky nahi).

Test `ejects after N consecutive failures, then lets the target back after ejectMs` 9,999 ms par check karta hai ki abhi bhi unavailable hai, phir 1 ms aur badha ke available. Yeh exact boundary (`now >= ejectedUntil`) test karta hai, jo real sleep se kabhi reliably nahi ho pata.

Yahi pattern HealthChecker mein bhi hai: probe function inject hoti hai (`probe` option) aur `checkOnce()` seedha call hota hai, timer ki jagah. Sirf kuch integration tests real timers par chalte hain (jaise health check interval 20 ms), aur woh `waitFor` helper se condition ka intezaar karte hain, fixed sleep se nahi. Is project ka sabak: time aur network ko dependency ki tarah inject karo.
why_needed: Time-based logic ka fast aur deterministic testing.
real_world_analogy: Cricket ke match ko practice mein 'time-lapse' mein khelna, asli ghanton intezaar kiye bina.
how_it_works: Dependency injection: time source ko parameter banao, tests apna controllable version dete hain.

disadvantages: Real timer wiring (setInterval) ko alag se test karna padta hai
common_mistakes: Real sleep se test likhna (slow aur flaky)
Boundary ko test na karna

question: Walk through the attempt loop in handle(): what happens on a failure, and what guards stop double handling?
answer_hinglish:
`attempt(avoid, previousError)` ek attempt chalata hai. Pehle purani lease release hoti hai (agar pichla attempt fail hua tha), phir `lb.acquire(avoid)` naya target deta hai. Agar kuch available nahi aur koi pichla error nahi toh 503; agar pichla error tha toh woh original error (502 ya 504) bhejte hain, kyunki client ke liye asli failure wahi tha. Phir `http.request` banti hai aur `up = request` set hota hai.

Failure par `request.on('error')` chalta hai. Guards: (1) `if (request !== up) return;` purane attempt ke late events ko ignore karta hai, taaki ek hi request ke liye do attempts na chal jayein. (2) `if (res.destroyed) return;` client ke ja chukne par kuch nahi karta aur upstream ko blame nahi karta. Phir `reportFailure()` (har attempt mein ek hi baar, `failureReported` flag se). Agar headers jaa chuke hain toh connection destroy, retry nahi. Warna agar `attempts < maxAttempts` aur error retryable hai toh `attempt(target, err)`, avoid ke saath, warna `sendError`.

Subtle: release hamesha `res.on('close')` par bhi hota hai, aur release idempotent hai, isliye dono jagah se release karna safe hai. Test `leaves every counter at zero after retried and failed requests` is poore loop ke baad counters check karta hai.
why_needed: Retry loop mein sabse zyada subtle bugs hote hain: double retry, leaked lease, galat blame.
real_world_analogy: Chitthi bhejne wala: pehla pata galat nikla toh doosre pate par bhejta hai, lekin pehle ko wapas receipt deta hai aur dono ko ginti mein nahi gina.
how_it_works: Recursion-jaisa loop: error handler hi agla attempt chalata hai. State (up, lease, attempts) closure mein hai.
in_this_project: proxy.ts::createProxy ke andar attempt(), isRetryable, sendError.
disadvantages: Closure state ko samajhna mushkil
Backoff aur retry budget nahi hai
common_mistakes: Purane attempt ke events ko ignore na karna
Failure ko ek hi attempt mein do baar count karna
follow_up_questions: Retry budget kaise jodoge?
Is loop ko async/await mein kaise likhoge, aur kya badlega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Event-driven nested attempts simple hain par state closure mein bikhri hai. Ek explicit state machine ya async function with AbortController zyada readable ho sakta hai, lekin streaming aur event ordering ke saath nazuk.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Late error ek purane attempt se: guard roakta hai. Dono request error aur response close ek hi failure ke liye fire: failureReported flag. Client abort beech mein: res.destroyed guard.
advanced.alternatives: Promise-based attempt function; library jaise undici ke retry interceptors; ek separate Retrier class.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par retries load multiply karti hain (worst case 1 + RETRIES guna). Global retry budget zaroori ho jata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Retry budget, jittered backoff, per-attempt metrics, aur attempts ka histogram.

question: Why can only body-less requests be replayed, and what would replaying a POST body require?
answer_hinglish:
Stage 1 ka design hai ki body memory mein jama nahi hoti: `req.pipe(up)` bytes ko seedha aage bhej deta hai aur bhool jata hai. Isliye jab attempt fail ho jaye, hamare paas wo bytes nahi bachte jo dobara bheje jaayein. Body-less request (GET bina body) mein bhejne ke liye kuch hai hi nahi, toh woh asani se replay ho sakti hai: `request.end()` aur bas.

POST ki body replay karne ke liye do tarike: (1) body ko buffer karo (memory mein ya disk par) pehle attempt ke saath saath, size limit ke saath; fail hone par dobara se bhejo. Nuksan: memory, latency, aur streaming ka fayda khatam. (2) Client se body dobara maango: possible nahi. Aur duplicate side effects ka masla alag hai (idempotency).

Is project ne dono choices tak jaane ke bajaye retry ko body-less safe methods tak seemit rakha: simple, safe, aur streaming bachi hui. `isReplayable` check method, `transfer-encoding` aur `content-length` teeno dekhta hai. Agar kabhi buffered retry chahiye, toh sirf chhoti bodies (jaise 64 KB tak) ke liye ek explicit option hona chahiye.
why_needed: Streaming ke design ke natije ko samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Live TV: jo nikal gaya woh wapas nahi aata; recorded show ko dobara chala sakte ho.
how_it_works: Streamed bytes consume ho jaate hain. Replay ke liye ya store karna padega ya source se dobara lena padega.
in_this_project: proxy.ts::isReplayable aur attempt() mein `if (replayable) request.end(); else req.pipe(request);`.
advantages: Streaming ka memory fayda bacha rehta hai
disadvantages: Uploads kabhi retry nahi hote
Kuch safe retries (PUT) chhoot jaati hain
common_mistakes: Body ko bina limit ke buffer karna
Content-Length ko ignore karna

question: The proxy probes /health on every upstream. Is it safe to leave that path reachable from the internet?
answer_hinglish:
Health endpoint kabhi kabhi andar ki jaankari deta hai: version, database connection ka status, build number. Agar woh public internet se reachable hai toh attacker ko free reconnaissance milti hai. Hamara proxy sirf request ko forward karta hai; woh /health par koi special rule nahi lagata. Matlab agar koi client proxy ke through `/health` maange, toh woh bhi upstream tak jayegi, aur app jo bhi dikhaye woh bahar dikhega. Maine is project mein /health ko block ya restrict nahi kiya hai.

Practical rules: (1) health endpoint par sirf `ok` jaisa minimal jawab ho, koi version ya internal details nahi. (2) Agar zyada details chahiye toh alag internal path rakho jo sirf private network se reachable ho. (3) Caddy ya proxy ke upar path-based rule se external /health ko block karna possible hai, lekin tab probes ko bhi proxy ke bajaye seedha upstream ke address par jaana hota hai, jo hamara HealthChecker karta hi hai (woh upstream URL par seedha request bhejta hai, proxy ke through nahi).

Ek aur point: probe ek real request ki tarah app tak jaati hai, toh app ke access logs mein har 5 second ek entry banegi. User-Agent `reverse-proxy-healthcheck` set hota hai taaki filter ho sake.
why_needed: Operational endpoints se information leak ya extra attack surface na bane.
real_world_analogy: Hospital ka 'staff only' register: darwaze par bahar waalon ko nahi dikhana chahiye.
how_it_works: Proxy generic forwarder hai: koi path special nahi. Probes upstream address par seedha jaate hain.
in_this_project: health.ts::httpProbe seedha upstream URL par jaata hai aur user-agent set karta hai. Proxy path filtering nahi karta.
code_example:
http.get({ hostname: base.hostname, port: base.port || 80, path, timeout: timeoutMs, agent: false,
  headers: { "user-agent": "reverse-proxy-healthcheck" } }, (res) => { /* 2xx/3xx healthy */ });
advantages: Probes seedha upstream par: proxy ke raaste nahi
disadvantages: Public /health ka leak proxy rokta nahi
Koi path-blocking option nahi

Sochna ki internal path hai toh safe hai

question: How can retries amplify an outage or an attack, and what bounds them here?
answer_hinglish:
Retry ek failing server par load badha deta hai. Agar upstream already struggle kar raha hai aur har failed request ek aur request bana de, toh load 2x ho jata hai, aur server aur gir jata hai: retry storm. Attacker ke liye bhi yeh amplification hai: ek request ka asar upstream par do requests jitna.

Is project mein bound: `retries` default 1, matlab ek request ke zyada se zyada 2 attempts. `RETRIES=0` se band. Aur sirf body-less GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, sirf connection-level failure par, sirf response ka ek bhi byte jaane se pehle. Response-idle timeout par retry nahi hota, kyunki wahi 'slow server' wala case hai jahan retry sabse zyada nuksan karta. Test `does not retry a response-idle timeout` isko pakadta hai.

Jo nahi hai: koi global retry budget (jaise 'sirf 10% requests retry ho sakti hain'), koi backoff ya jitter. Toh worst case total load 1 + RETRIES guna ho sakta hai. Production ke liye budget zaroor chahiye. Maine koi load test nahi kiya jo retry storm dikhaye, isliye yeh design reasoning hai, measured nahi.
why_needed: Resilience feature ko outage amplifier banne se rokna.
real_world_analogy: Sab log ek band darwaze par baar baar dhakka marein toh darwaza aur jam hota hai.

question: Health state is per proxy process. What inconsistencies and costs does that create?
answer_hinglish:
Har proxy process ka apna `Balancer`, apne counters, apna health state aur (agar on ho) apna HealthChecker hai. Multiple processes ya multiple proxies hon toh: (1) Views alag ho sakte hain: process 1 ne B ko down mana, process 2 abhi bhi use bhej raha hai, kyunki uske probes ya failures abhi us tak pahunche nahi. Thodi der ke liye traffic inconsistent rehta hai. (2) Probe load multiply hota hai: 4 processes x N upstreams x har 5 second. (3) Recovery par sab processes ek saath wapas bhejte hain, toh ek naya wapas aaya server achanak poora traffic le sakta hai (thundering herd), kyunki slow start nahi hai.

Options: ek hi health checker service jo state share kare (extra component, extra failure point); probes ko ek process tak seemit karna aur result baanta; ya sab ko apna kaam karne dena aur thodi inconsistency accept karna jab tak scale chhota ho.

Abhi hamare paas single process hai, toh yeh sirf design discussion hai. README mein bhi likha hai ki health state per process hai. Probe load ya herd effect ka koi measurement maine nahi kiya.
why_needed: Scale badhne par local decisions ke nateeje samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Har guard apni alag register rakhe: ek ko lagta hai gate band hai, doosre ko abhi bhi khula.
how_it_works: State process memory mein hai. Koi gossip ya shared store nahi.
in_this_project: balancer.ts state fields (healthy, failures, ejectedUntil); health.ts HealthChecker per Balancer.
advantages: Ek process ka failure doosre ko affect nahi karta
disadvantages: Inconsistent views
Probe load multiply
Recovery par herd effect
common_mistakes: Sochna ki sab processes ka view hamesha same hoga
Probe load ko ignore karna
follow_up_questions: Slow start kaise implement karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Local state: simple, resilient to shared-store failure, approximate. Shared state: consistent, but ek aur component aur latency. Chhote scale par local hi theek.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Ek process ka network partition akele: woh sab upstreams ko down maan sakta hai (false positives) jabki baaki theek. Recovery par herd: naya upstream ek saath overwhelm.
advanced.alternatives: Centralised health service (jaise Consul), xDS-style control plane, probe sharding, ek leader jo probe kare.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x processes par probe load 10x; probe sharding ya shared service zaroori. 100x par control plane.

question: Why does HealthChecker skip a round if the previous one is still running?
answer_hinglish:
Probe round mein har upstream ko request jaati hai aur har probe ka timeout hota hai (default 2 second). Agar interval 5 second ho aur kuch upstreams hung hon, toh ek round 2 second tak chal sakta hai, jo interval se chhota hai: theek. Lekin agar kisi configuration mein timeout ya network delay interval se bada ho jaye (jaise interval 1 second, timeout 2 second), toh agla round pichle round khatam hone se pehle shuru ho jata, aur rounds ek ke upar ek jama hote jaate: har round ke saath zyada concurrent probes, zyada sockets, aur aur zyada slow.

`roundRunning` flag yeh rokta hai: `round()` shuru mein check karta hai, agar pichla abhi chal raha hai toh seedha return (us round ko skip). `finally` mein flag false hota hai, taaki exception par bhi flag atke nahi.

Yeh `setInterval` ka classic sabak hai: setInterval pichle callback ke khatam hone ka intezaar nahi karta. Is behaviour ka alag unit test maine nahi likha; code mein guard hai aur yeh reasoning hai. Agar test likhna ho toh ek probe jo manually resolve ho aur do `round()` calls ke baad dekhna ki probe sirf ek baar chali.
why_needed: Overlapping async jobs se resource pile-up rokna.
real_world_analogy: Ek safai karmchari ka round abhi khatam nahi hua aur doosra round shuru ho gaya: kaam ek ke upar ek jama hota jaata.
how_it_works: Boolean guard + try/finally. setInterval ke callbacks overlap kar sakte hain jab callback async ho.

question: What does the proxy do when every upstream is unhealthy, and what is the alternative design?
answer_hinglish:
Jab saare upstreams unavailable hain (unhealthy ya ejected), `acquire()` `NoHealthyUpstreamError` throw karta hai aur proxy 503 'No Healthy Upstream' deta hai, `Retry-After: 1` ke saath, upstream ko call kiye bina. Fayda: client ko turant saaf jawab, aur mare hue servers par bekar connection attempts nahi.

Alternative 'panic mode' hai (Envoy jaisa): jab sab unhealthy dikhein, toh health information ko galat maan ke traffic phir bhi sab ko bhej do. Soch yeh hai ki agar health checking hi galat ho (jaise /health endpoint ek bug se 500 de raha hai jabki app theek hai, ya network blip se saare probes fail ho gaye), toh 503 de ke poori site down karna health system ki galti se outage ban jata hai. Panic mode mein shayad kuch requests chal jaati.

Humne 503 chuna kyunki saaf aur simple hai, aur honest hai. Trade-off yeh hai ki ek galat health check poori site ko 503 de sakta hai. Test `answers 503 with Retry-After when no upstream is available` is behaviour ko pakadta hai. Panic mode implement nahi hai, README mein bhi 'Not implemented' mein likha hai.

real_world_analogy: Sab lifts 'out of order' dikhein toh bhi ek ki wiring check kar lo: shayad board hi galat ho.

question: What is the stale keep-alive connection problem, and how do retries and the same-target fallback address it?
answer_hinglish:
Hamara proxy upstream ke saath keep-alive connections pool mein rakhta hai. Upstream (Node ka default keepAliveTimeout 5 second) idle connection ko band kar deta hai. Race: proxy ek pooled connection ko usi pal use karne laga jab upstream use band kar raha tha. Nateeja: request bheji, lekin connection toot gaya bina jawab ke: ECONNRESET. Upstream bilkul theek hai, bas connection purana tha.

Fix: retry. GET (body-less) ke liye `ECONNRESET` retryable hai. Retry ek naya connection kholta hai aur chal jata hai. Aur kyunki ek hi upstream ho sakta hai, `acquire(avoid)` mein rule hai: doosra available target ho toh use prefer karo, warna usi ko dobara allow karo. Isi liye ek upstream wali setup mein bhi retry kaam karti hai.

Test `recovers from a connection the upstream reset before answering, even with ONE upstream` first request par socket destroy karwata hai aur doosri par jawab deta hai: client ko 200 milta hai, attempts 2. Stage 4 mein race asli roop mein reproduce hui (PROXY-086): ek raw server jo 200 ms idle ke baad connection band karta hai aur Keep-Alive hint nahi bhejta; 300 requests mein retries off par 1 request ko 502 ECONNRESET mila, retries 1 par 2 resets hue aur dono retry ho gaye (client ko 300 x 200). Node upstream (jo Keep-Alive: timeout hint bhejta hai) ke saath 300 mein koi reset nahi hua. Race rare hai: yeh production rate nahi batata. Aur POST par yeh help nahi karta: woh retry nahi hota.
why_needed: Ek aam production error (random ECONNRESET) ko samajhna aur handle karna.
real_world_analogy: Purana phone line: aap number milate ho aur line pehle hi kat chuki thi; dobara dial karne par sab theek.
how_it_works: Pooled socket par request likhne se pehle upstream FIN bhej chuka hota hai ya usi waqt bhejta hai. Naya connection khulna chahiye.
in_this_project: proxy.ts::isRetryable (ECONNRESET), balancer.ts::acquire(avoid) fallback, test resilience.test.ts.
code_example: const RETRYABLE_CODES = new Set(["ECONNREFUSED", "ECONNRESET", "EPIPE", "EHOSTUNREACH", "ENETUNREACH", "EAI_AGAIN", "ENOTFOUND"]);
advantages: Random resets user tak nahi pahunchte (GET ke liye)
disadvantages: POST ko help nahi
Race rare hai aur sirf no-hint upstream par reproduce hua
Failure ek ejection count bhi bana sakta hai

Retry ke bina keep-alive use karna

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Retry (reactive) ya agent idle timeout ko upstream se chhota rakhna (proactive). Dono ka combination best: proactive se race kam, retry se bacha hua cover.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Reset ke baad retry bhi fail ho (upstream sach mein down): 502 ke saath failure ejection ki taraf count hota hai. POST par reset: client ko 502, duplicate risk ke bina.
advanced.alternatives: Keep-alive band karna (slow), HTTP/2 upstream, undici pool ka built-in reconnect.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par race zyada baar hit hota hai; agent timeout tune aur reset ka metric zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: Agent ka freeSocketTimeout upstream se kam, ECONNRESET ka alag counter (stale vs real failure), aur POST ke liye idempotency keys.

question: An upstream is slow, not dead. Why does the proxy answer 504 without retrying, and what protects the other servers?
answer_hinglish:
Slow upstream aur dead upstream alag problems hain. Dead: connection turant refuse, retry doosre server par jaldi kaam aata hai. Slow: server zinda hai lekin jawab dheere de raha hai, shayad overload ke wajah se. Agar hum timeout par retry karte, toh (1) client ko double wait: 30 second timeout + doosre server ka time, (2) overloaded server par ek aur request ka bojh, aur (3) agar sab servers slow hain toh retries se sab par load 2x.

Isliye `isRetryable` `UpstreamTimeoutError` ke liye false deta hai aur client ko 504 milta hai. Test `does not retry a response-idle timeout (slow is not unreachable)` check karta hai ki doosra upstream ko ek bhi request nahi gayi.

Connect timeout (3 second default) alag hai: agar TCP connection hi nahi ban raha toh woh 'unreachable' hai, aur retry theek hai (`ConnectTimeoutError` retryable hai). Aur passive health slow servers ko eject bhi karti hai: idle timeout `reportFailure` ko count karta hai, toh baar baar timeout hone par server rotation se hat jata hai. Dhyan: yeh thresholds maine real slow server par measure nahi kiye.
why_needed: Slow server par aur load daalne se bachna.
real_world_analogy: Ek dheere cashier ke saath customer ko wapas line mein khada karna aur aur lamba intezaar nahi dilana chahiye.
how_it_works: Error classes: ConnectTimeoutError (retryable), UpstreamTimeoutError (not retryable).

if (err instanceof ConnectTimeoutError) return true;
if (err instanceof UpstreamTimeoutError) return false;

question: A half-broken upstream fails every other request. What does this design do, and what would catch it?
answer_hinglish:
Maan lo ek upstream har doosri request par connection reset deta hai. Passive ejection 'consecutive' failures par chalta hai: fail, success, fail, success: streak baar baar 0 ho jati hai, toh woh kabhi eject nahi hota. Test `failures must be consecutive on real traffic: a success in between keeps the upstream in rotation` yahi dikhata hai: statuses [502, 200, 502, 200, ...], kabhi 503 nahi, kyunki target kabhi eject nahi hua.

Is design ka asar: GET requests ke liye retry (default 1) failures ko chhupa leti hai, kyunki fail ke baad retry kisi aur target par ya usi par success ho sakti hai. Lekin POST ko 50% error milega. Aur woh server rotation mein hi rehta hai. Active health check bhi isko nahi pakadega agar uska /health pass ho jaye.

Jo isko pakadega: success-rate based outlier detection: pichle N requests mein failure percentage dekho (jaise 50% se zyada) aur eject karo. Yeh implement nahi hai. Yeh ek aur trade-off hai consecutive rule ka: simple aur false positives se bachata hai, lekin 'partially failing' servers ko miss karta hai. Maine yeh limitation test mein document ki hai, fix nahi kiya.
why_needed: Consecutive-failure rule ki seemayein samajhna.
real_world_analogy: Ek kharab bulb jo aadhe time jalta hai: tab tak koi nahi badalta jab tak woh poori tarah bujh na jaye.
how_it_works: Consecutive counter success par reset ho jata hai: alternate failures kabhi threshold tak nahi pahunchte.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::reportSuccess reset; test resilience.test.ts failures must be consecutive.

[502, 200, 502, 200, 502, 200]  // never 503: it is never ejected
disadvantages: Partial failures miss
POST ko 50% errors
Success-rate detection nahi hai
common_mistakes: Consecutive rule ko complete protection samajhna
Retries se partial failures chhupna aur dikhna band hona

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Consecutive: simple, kam false positives, partial failures miss. Success-rate: partial failures pakadta hai, lekin window size, minimum request volume aur flapping ka tuning chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Flaky NIC ya overloaded server jo intermittent resets deta hai: poora ejection kabhi nahi, error rate ongoing.
advanced.alternatives: Rolling window success rate, EWMA error rate, Envoy-style outlier detection with max ejection percent.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par statistical detection zyada reliable hoti hai; low traffic par noisy.
advanced.production_improvements: Per-upstream error-rate metric, success-rate ejection, aur retry-attempt logs ko alert se jodna (attempts > 1 ka ratio).

question: How would you choose ejectAfter, ejectMs, the probe interval and the thresholds? What did you actually measure?
answer_hinglish:
Honest jawab pehle: stage 4 mein maine kuch behaviours measure kiye (E3 kill under load, E5 black hole), lekin in defaults ko production traffic ke liye tune nahi kiya. Defaults (ejectAfter 3, ejectMs 10 second, probe interval 5 second, timeout 2 second, thresholds 2 aur 2, connect timeout 3 second, retries 1) sochi-samjhi shuruaati values hain, tuned nahi.

Tuning ka tareeka: detection time ka hisaab. Passive: ejectAfter requests ke baad turant, toh traffic jitna zyada utni jaldi. Active: interval x unhealthyThreshold, yani 5 x 2 = 10 second tak. Recovery time: active mein interval x healthyThreshold; passive mein ejectMs. Bahut chhota ejectMs matlab mara hua server baar baar try hota hai aur users ko failures; bahut bada matlab theek ho chuka server der tak bekaar. Chhota interval matlab zyada probe load; bada matlab slow detection.

Probe timeout ko /health ke normal latency se kaafi upar rakho, warna slow ho gaya server galat down mark hoga. Connect timeout same data-centre mein kuch seconds kaafi hain. Sahi tareeka: apne service ke asli SLO aur failure data (kitne seconds ki outage tolerable) se numbers nikalna, aur chaos test se verify karna. Stage 4 ke data ke baad koi default nahi badla (README ka 'Defaults after measuring' dekho).

real_world_analogy: Smoke alarm ki sensitivity: bahut tez toh roz galat alarm, bahut dheema toh aag ka der se pata.

question: Why retry only before the first response byte, and what are the alternatives?
answer_hinglish:
Jab tak client ko ek bhi response byte nahi gaya, request ka 'abhi tak kuch nahi hua' wala state hai: naya attempt kisi aur server par safely ho sakta hai, client ko pata bhi nahi chalega. Jaise hi headers (status line) client ko likh diye, hum committed hain: client ne status 200 aur kuch bytes dekh liye. Ab retry karne par ya toh purane bytes dobara jayenge (corruption) ya hum bytes ko skip karne ki koshish karenge (complex, range jaisa logic). Isliye `res.headersSent` ke baad hum retry nahi karte; connection destroy karte hain taaki client ko failure dikhe.

Alternatives: (1) Pehle poora response buffer karna, taaki fail hone par retry ho sake: streaming aur memory ka nuksan. (2) Hedged requests: slow hone par doosre server ko bhi parallel request bhejo aur jo pehle jawab de woh lo: tail latency ghatati hai lekin load badhati hai. (3) Range requests se resume: sirf tab jab upstream Range support kare.

Is project mein sabse simple safe choice hai. Test `never retries once response bytes have reached the client (mid-body failure)` check karta hai ki upstream ko ek hi baar hit mila aur doosre ko kuch nahi.

real_world_analogy: Parcel ko dukaan se nikalne se pehle badla ja sakta hai; customer ke haath mein aane ke baad nahi.

question: Walk through isRetryable and isReplayable and explain each condition.
answer_hinglish:
`isReplayable(req)` decide karta hai ki request ko dobara bheja ja sakta hai ya nahi. Teen conditions: (1) method sirf GET, HEAD ya OPTIONS ho (safe methods). (2) `transfer-encoding` header na ho (chunked body ka matlab body hai). (3) `content-length` ya toh absent ho ya '0'. Teeno true toh replayable. Agar replayable hai toh `req.resume()` se body drain hoti hai aur `request.end()` se upstream ko request poori bheji jati hai.

`isRetryable(err)` error ko dekhta hai: `ConnectTimeoutError` true (connection hi nahi bana, unreachable). Baaki `UpstreamTimeoutError` (idle timeout) false (slow, unreachable nahi). Warna error ka `code` ek fixed set mein ho: ECONNREFUSED (kuch listen nahi kar raha), ECONNRESET (connection toota), EPIPE, EHOSTUNREACH, ENETUNREACH, EAI_AGAIN aur ENOTFOUND (DNS ya network). Class ke order ka matlab hai: ConnectTimeoutError UpstreamTimeoutError ka subclass hai, isliye pehle usko check karna zaroori hai.

Dono functions pure hain aur chhote, toh unko alag se samajhna aur badalna aasan hai. `retries` option aur `maxAttempts = 1 + (replayable ? retries : 0)` dono ko jod ke final rule banate hain.
why_needed: Retry policy ko code mein padhne aur justify karne ki practice.
real_world_analogy: Courier ke rules: kaunsa parcel dobara bheja ja sakta hai (replayable), aur kaunsi galti par dobara koshish karni chahiye (retryable).

question: Users report intermittent 502s, but one of two upstreams looks healthy. How do you investigate?
answer_hinglish:
Pehla kadam: logs mein `status: 502` wali lines filter karo aur `upstream` field dekho: kaun sa upstream? Agar sab ek hi upstream ka hai toh wahi problem hai, aur agar `attempts: 2` hai toh retry bhi chala aur phir bhi fail hua (matlab retry bhi usi ya doosre bimaar server par gaya, ya request GET nahi thi). Agar request POST hai toh retry hota hi nahi, toh ek bimaar upstream par seedha 502 milega.

Doosra: health events dekho: `{"msg":"health", ...}` lines. Kya wo upstream kabhi eject hua? Agar nahi, toh shayad failures consecutive nahi hain (partial failure: har doosri request fail, ejection kabhi nahi, jaisa PROXY-063 mein hai). Test is behaviour ko dikhata hai.

Teesra: kya active health check on hai (`activeHealthCheck` startup log mein)? Agar nahi, toh ek bimaar server tab tak rotation mein rahega jab tak passive ejection na ho. Chautha: error ka asli reason: abhi 502 ke reason (ECONNREFUSED ya ECONNRESET) log mein nahi aata, sirf status. Yeh ek logging gap hai: reason field add karna ek improvement hai. Upstream ke apne logs aur `ss -tn` se connection state dekhna padega.

question: An upstream flips between healthy and unhealthy every few seconds. What do you check?
answer_hinglish:
Flapping ke symptoms: logs mein baar baar `{"msg":"health","healthy":false}` aur phir `true`, alternate. Pehle dekho kaun sa mechanism flip kar raha hai: reason field mein '2 health checks failed' (active) ya 'ejected for ... ms after ... failures' (passive).

Active flapping ke aam reasons: (1) probe timeout (default 2 second) /health ke asli latency se kam ya borderline hai: jab server thoda busy ho toh probe timeout ho jata hai. (2) Threshold 2 ka matlab do lagatar probes: agar server periodically (jaise GC ya cron job) 5 second ke liye atakta hai, toh dono probes fail ho sakte hain. (3) /health endpoint khud ek slow dependency (DB) par depend karta hai. Fix: timeout badhao, endpoint ko halka karo, ya thresholds badhao (healthyThreshold ko zyada rakho taaki wapas aane mein sabr ho).

Passive flapping: `ejectMs` ke baad server wapas aata hai, ek trial request fail hoti hai aur dobara eject: har 10 second ka cycle. Matlab server sach mein kharab hai; yeh flapping nahi, correct behavior hai. Fix server ka karo. Hamare paas abhi flapping ko rokne ke liye alag hysteresis (jaise ejectMs ka badhna) nahi hai.
why_needed: Health system ke apne oscillations ko debug karna.

question: How do health checks interact with a rolling deploy of the upstream apps, and what is still missing?
answer_hinglish:
Rolling deploy mein ek ek karke upstream restart hota hai. Jab upstream band hota hai, toh uski requests fail honge. Health checks se: restart ke dauran probes fail honge, do lagatar fail ke baad (default 10 second ke andar) proxy use rotation se hata dega. Is beech passive ejection aur retries kaam aate hain: GET requests doosre upstream par chali jaati hain aur users ko error nahi dikhta (agar doosra healthy hai).

Jo missing hai: draining. Behtar flow yeh hota ki deploy script pehle upstream ko 'drain' mark kare (naye requests band, chalti requests poori hon) aur phir restart kare. Abhi proxy ke paas aisa koi control nahi hai, toh restart ke dauran in-flight requests (jo already upstream par thi) toot sakti hain, aur POST/uploads ko retry nahi milti. App side par graceful shutdown (SIGTERM par naye connections band, chalti requests poori) is gap ko kam kar sakta hai.

Wapas aane par: jab restart hoke upstream /health pass kare (2 lagatar pass), woh wapas rotation mein aata hai. Slow start nahi hai, toh use turant poora share milta hai, jabki cold app (cache khali) dheere chal sakta hai. Maine rolling deploy ka end to end test nahi kiya.
why_needed: Deploys ke time availability banaye rakhna.
real_world_analogy: Ek ek khambe ko badalte hue pul par traffic jaari rakhna: pehle ek taraf band, kaam, phir doosri.
how_it_works: Probes failure detect karte hain, passive ejection tezi se react karti hai, retries GET ko bachati hain.
in_this_project: health.ts, balancer.ts, proxy.ts retries. Missing: draining.
advantages: GET traffic deploy ke dauran bachti hai
disadvantages: In-flight aur POST requests toot sakti hain

question: What do health checks, retries and the connect timeout cost, and what have you not measured?
answer_hinglish:
Probe cost: har round mein har upstream ko ek HTTP request, ek naye connection par (`agent: false`): handshake plus request. N upstreams, interval 5 second: har proxy process se N requests har 5 second. Chhote N par yeh negligible hai, lekin multiple processes ya bahut chhote interval par yeh multiply hota hai (PROXY-058). Probe asli app ko bhi hit karta hai, toh /health halka hona chahiye.

Retry cost: worst case ek failing request 1 + RETRIES upstream attempts leti hai, aur latency bhi badhti hai: connect timeout (3 second) tak ek attempt, phir doosra. Isliye connect timeout chhota rakhna latency ke liye zaroori hai. Per-request overhead: ek lease aur kuch closures, mamooli, lekin maine koi CPU ya latency measure nahi ki.

Connect timeout: ek timer har naye connection par (reused socket par nahi), toh keep-alive pool ke saath yeh timer kam hi lagta hai. Test sirf correctness check karta hai.

Honest summary: stage 4 mein throughput aur latency measure hue (PROXY-077), lekin probe-load, retry ka tail latency par asar aur per-process CPU measure nahi hue: woh ab bhi sirf reasoning hai.
why_needed: Resilience features ke cost ko jaanna aur measure karne ka plan.
real_world_analogy: Smoke detectors ki battery aur testing ka kharcha: suraksha ke liye zaroori par free nahi.
how_it_works: Probe: N x (1/interval) requests per second per proxy. Retry: extra attempts x latency.
in_this_project: health.ts::httpProbe; proxy.ts retries; connect.ts::watchConnect.
advantages: Optional features (health check off by default)
disadvantages: Probe cost aur per-process CPU measure nahi hue
Probe load multi-process mein multiply
common_mistakes: Bina measure ke 'negligible' bolna
Probe interval bahut chhota rakhna
follow_up_questions: Probe load ko kaise measure karoge?
Retries ka tail latency par asar kaise measure karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Zyada checks = jaldi detection par zyada load; retries = availability par load aur latency. Har ek ko budget ke saath chalana chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Probes khud server par load daalein jab woh already struggle kar raha ho; retry storm.
advanced.alternatives: Passive-only health (koi probe load nahi), probe sharding, longer intervals.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x upstreams par probe volume 10x: sharding ya shared checker. 100x par control plane.
advanced.production_improvements: Probe metrics, retry-rate metric, connect timeout ko network RTT se tune karna, aur stage 4 ka load test.

question: Should health state survive a proxy restart? What would persisting it involve?
answer_hinglish:
Hamare design mein health state memory mein hai aur restart par khatam: har target `healthy: true`, `failures: 0` se shuru hota hai (optimistic). Active checks agar on hain toh turant ek round chalta hai (`start()` mein) aur 2 lagatar fail par mare hue server ko 10 second ke andar hata deta hai. Passive ejection restart par bhool jata hai, toh ek mare hue server ko dobara 3 failures chahiye.

Persist karna chahiye? Aam taur par nahi. Health state bahut jaldi purani ho jati hai (seconds), toh restart ke baad file se padha hua 'down' ya 'up' shayad ab galat ho. Galat 'down' persisted ho toh ek theek server hata rahega jab tak probes use theek na karein; galat 'up' persisted ho toh mara hua server milega. Optimistic start + fast detection simpler aur safe hai.

Agar kabhi state share ya persist karna ho (multi-process), toh yeh ek short-TTL data hai (jaise Redis key with TTL), durable database nahi: har entry ka expiry 2 se 3 probe intervals ho. Config (upstream list) alag cheez hai aur woh file ya store mein rahegi. Abhi yeh sirf design discussion hai, koi persistence code nahi hai.
why_needed: State ke lifetime ke hisaab se uska ghar chunna.
real_world_analogy: Mausam ki report subah ki chhapi hui akhbaar mein: shaam tak purani; live thermometer dekhna behtar.
how_it_works: Short-lived state ko TTL ke saath ya memory mein; durable store sirf slow-changing config ke liye.

{ url, active: 0, healthy: true, failures: 0, ejectedUntil: 0 }

question: Design health checking and failover for the planned Oracle setup (proxy on one server, apps on another).
answer_hinglish:
Layout: Caddy -> proxy (A2) -> apps (A1). Health checks ko design karte waqt: (1) Probe path: apps par ek halka `/health` jo sirf 'process zinda hai aur request le sakta hai' bataye. Deep check (DB ping) ka khatra: agar database ek second ke liye atak jaye toh saare app servers ek saath unhealthy ho jayenge aur proxy 503 dega: ek dependency ka outage poori site ka outage ban jata hai. Isliye shallow check chuno aur dependencies ke liye alag monitoring rakho.

(2) Network: A1 ke app ports sirf A2 ke IP ke liye Oracle security list mein khulein; probes bhi usi raaste se jaate hain. (3) Settings: `HEALTH_PATH=/health`, interval 5 second, 2 aur 2 thresholds se ~10 second mein detect; `RETRIES=1` GET ke liye; `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS=3000`, jo same-region network ke liye zyada hai aur chhota kiya ja sakta hai. (4) Monitoring: health events ke logs, 502/503/504 ka count, aur `attempts > 1` ka ratio.

Honest status: yeh deploy nahi hua; stage 4 hai. Do app servers ka setup bhi abhi nahi hai: A1 par ek hi server hai, toh 'failover' ke liye pehle doosra app instance chahiye (same server par do processes ya doosra server). Single points of failure: proxy aur Caddy khud, dono ke liye HA nahi hai.
why_needed: Component ko asli infrastructure ke context mein fit karna.
real_world_analogy: Do dukaanon wali gali: gali ka guard (proxy) dekhta hai kaun si dukaan khuli hai, par guard aur gali ka gate khud band ho jaye toh sab band.
how_it_works: Shallow probe, network allow-list, thresholds se detection time, aur monitoring.

HEALTH_PATH=/health HEALTH_INTERVAL_MS=5000 RETRIES=1 CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS=1000

Network allow-list se attack surface chhota
disadvantages: Abhi deploy nahi hua

question: How does this ejection design relate to a circuit breaker, and what would success-rate outlier detection add?
answer_hinglish:
Circuit breaker ke teen states hote hain: closed (normal), open (calls roki hui), half-open (kuch trial calls). Hamari passive ejection isi ki per-upstream, time-based shakal hai: normal = available; ejected = open (ejectMs ke liye skip); ejection ke baad ka ek trial = half-open (`failures = ejectAfter - 1` trick). Farak: traditional circuit breaker aksar client ki taraf se ek downstream service ke liye hota hai aur failure rate ya latency dekhta hai; hamara upstream pool ke andar ek ek server par laga hai aur sirf consecutive connection failures dekhta hai.

Success-rate outlier detection (Envoy jaisa) kya add karta: har target ka rolling window (jaise pichle 100 requests), aur agar success rate threshold se kam ho (jaise 50 percent) toh eject, saath mein 'ek saath kitne percent targets eject ho sakte hain' ki limit (taaki sab eject na ho jayein). Yeh PROXY-063 ke partial failure case ko pakadta hai, jo consecutive rule miss karta hai.

Cost: window ka state, minimum request volume (kam traffic par noisy), tuning. Yeh abhi implement nahi hai. Yeh ek achha next improvement hai, aur 'max ejection percent' ki limit ek important safety feature hai jo abhi hamare paas nahi: agar sab targets ek saath eject hon toh 503.
why_needed: Resilience patterns ko ek doosre se jodna aur agla step pehchanna.
real_world_analogy: Bijli ka fuse: trip (open), thodi der baad ek test try (half-open), theek toh wapas (closed).
how_it_works: Ejection = open. Time ke baad pehla failure ya success = half-open decision. Success par closed.
in_this_project: balancer.ts::reportFailure, reportSuccess; PROXY-063 ka test.
advantages: Half-open trick extra state ke bina
disadvantages: Success-rate detection nahi
Max ejection percent ki limit nahi

Bina 'max ejection' limit ke aggressive ejection

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Consecutive failures: simple, false positives kam. Success-rate: partial failures pakadta hai par tuning aur volume chahiye. Dono ek saath bhi ho sakte hain.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Zyada aggressive ejection saare servers eject kar sakta hai (cascading). Max ejection limit is risk ko roakti hai.
advanced.alternatives: EWMA based, latency-based ejection, gradual weight reduction instead of binary ejection.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par rolling windows reliable; kam traffic par minimum-volume rule zaroori.
advanced.production_improvements: Rolling success-rate ejection, max ejection percent, panic threshold, aur events ke saath metrics.

question: Write a test proving that a POST without a body is NOT retried even though it has nothing to replay.
answer_hinglish:
Yeh test ek aisi galti pakadta hai jo pehle meri apni test suite se chhoot gayi thi. Pehle ka POST test body ke saath tha, aur body wali request `content-length` ki wajah se replayable hi nahi thi: toh method ki checking hata dene par bhi woh test pass hota raha. Maine mutation se yeh gap pakda: method check hatane par koi test fail nahi hua. Isliye body-less POST ka test zaroori hai.

Plan: do upstreams: ek dead port, aur ek counting upstream. Round-robin mein pehli request dead ko jayegi. `fetch(url, { method: "POST" })` (bina body ke) bhejo aur assert karo ki status 502 hai: agar retry hota toh live par jaake 200 milta. Phir ek `DELETE` bhejo: round-robin ab live par jayega aur 200 aayega, aur live ke hits ko 1 hona chahiye (ek hi real request, retry ki wajah se extra nahi).

Method check hata ke test chalane par woh fail hota hai (maine verify kiya). Test `a POST with NO body is still not retried` resilience.test.ts mein hai.
why_needed: Ek asli test gap ko pehchan ke band karna.
real_world_analogy: Safety check ka ek asli test: sirf seat-belt lagane ka nahi, belt na lagane par alarm bajne ka bhi.
how_it_works: Counting upstream se verify karte hain ki retry ne doosre server ko chhua ya nahi.
in_this_project: test/resilience.test.ts mein hai; helpers.ts mein countingUpstream.
disadvantages: Test dead port helper par depend karta hai (race ka chhota risk, isliye files serial chalti hain)

Test ko kabhi fail hote hue na dekhna

question: Sketch a global retry budget so retries can never exceed a fraction of normal traffic.
answer_hinglish:
Problem: abhi har request ke liye zyada se zyada `RETRIES` extra attempts hain, lekin agar sab requests fail ho rahi hain toh load 1 + RETRIES guna ho jata hai. Retry budget kehta hai: retries kul requests ke ek fraction (jaise 10 percent) se zyada nahi ho sakti.

Sketch: ek chhota counter object: `requests` (kul aayi) aur `retries` (kul retried), ek rolling window mein (jaise pichle 10 second). `attempt()` mein retry karne se pehle `budget.tryRetry()` poochho: yeh true deta hai agar `retries + 1 <= 0.1 * requests` (aur kam se kam kuch minimum retries allowed ho, jaise 3 per window, taaki low traffic par budget 0 na ho). Warna retry skip aur seedha error. Window ko ring buffer ya do buckets se banao, timestamp ke saath.

Test: fake clock ke saath: 100 requests ke baad sirf 10 retries allow honi chahiye, window slide hone par naye. Yeh sketch hai, repo mein implement nahi hai, aur README ke 'Not implemented' mein budget listed hai. Jab implement karenge toh pehle integration test likhna: sab upstreams dead hon, 100 GET bhejo, aur upstream ko kul attempts 110 se zyada na milein.
why_needed: Retry storms ko design se bound karna.
real_world_analogy: Bank mein overdraft limit: ek seema tak hi udhaar, taaki ek galti poora account na dubaye.
how_it_works: Rolling-window ratio check retry se pehle. Fake clock se testable.
in_this_project: Not implemented. Extension point: proxy.ts::createProxy attempt() mein retry decision.
disadvantages: Window state aur tuning
Per-process budget (global nahi)
common_mistakes: Budget ko per-request rakhna
Minimum retries ke bina low traffic par budget 0
follow_up_questions: Budget ko per upstream kaise rakhoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Strict budget storms rokta hai par kuch legit retries drop kar sakta hai. Zyada budget availability deta hai par amplification risk.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Poori outage mein budget khatam: retries band, errors seedhe users ko. Yeh jaan boojh ke design hai.
advanced.alternatives: Token bucket for retries, adaptive concurrency limits, jittered backoff.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Multi-process mein per-process budget global se zyada de sakta hai; shared ya conservative per-process values chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Budget exhaustion metric, per-upstream budgets, aur jittered backoff.
